That’s wonderful to hear! Meal-prepping can be such a satisfying way to set yourself up for a smoother week, especially when you’re experimenting with new recipes. Here are some tips to help streamline your process—even as you try out new dishes:

**1. Batch Your Prep Steps:**  
Group similar tasks together (chopping all veggies at once, cooking all grains/legumes together, etc.), regardless of which recipe they’re for. This minimizes cleanup and keeps you in a flow.

**2. Mise en Place for Experiments:**  
Before you start, lay out all ingredients for your new recipes. This helps you spot missing items and makes the actual cooking smoother, especially when you’re following unfamiliar steps.

**3. Use a “Master Prep List”:**  
Create a single checklist for the week’s meals, breaking down each dish into prep steps. Highlight any overlapping ingredients or techniques (e.g., if two recipes use roasted chickpeas, roast a big batch at once).

**4. Document Tweaks as You Go:**  
Keep your wellness journal or a digital note open while you cook. Jot down quick thoughts on what worked, what didn’t, and ideas for next time—this saves you from trying to remember details later.

**5. Prep Versatile Components:**  
When experimenting, prep some “base” ingredients (like cooked lentils, grains, or roasted veggies) that can be used in multiple dishes. This gives you flexibility if a new recipe doesn’t turn out as planned.

**6. Clean as You Go:**  
Tidy up between steps or while something’s simmering/roasting. It keeps your workspace clear and makes the whole process feel less overwhelming.

**7. Set a Timer or Playlist:**  
Time-box your prep session or play a favorite playlist. It can make the process feel more enjoyable and help you stay focused.

**8. Save “Recipe Cards” for Favorites:**  
When you land on a recipe you love (even with tweaks), save a simplified version in a digital note or app. Over time, you’ll build a personal library of go-to meals that are easy to repeat.
